scope: Read-only attribution of existing ordinary Windows 3.11 60M V8 and mode-clock profiles. No new run or emulator change.

separateModeClockEvidence.zeroCost16BitCeiling: About 3.31x to 3.35x for this workload, before profiler overhead.

interpretation: The V8 self-sample totals are not mode-specific. The separate mode-clock runs show that about 70% of attributed user CPU belongs to real, protected16, or VM86 entry-mode step calls. A broad 16-bit block path needs to retire useful multi-instruction work while amortizing ordinary per-instruction step, decode, fetch, and translation work, with exact fault and device-event boundaries. The two profile percentages must not be multiplied or presented as a measured backend speedup; mode-clock attribution also includes board work.
